summary: Georgia's tower list places a 'macon' tower in Bibb County at elevation 515 (read as feet, about 157 m; the list gives no unit); no source describes its build, staffing, status or site today.

evidence.supports: List entry for the 'macon' tower: coordinates, county, elevation and tag gfc-601
The page says names for towers numbered 73 and above are the author's own
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: The list's map was last revised in March 2016
In 1956 the Georgia Forestry Commission and Georgia Forest Research Council moved state headquarters from Atlanta to Macon
evidence.quote: In 1956, the Georgia Forestry Commission and Georgia Forest Research Council moved state headquarters from Atlanta to Macon

sources.title: History of the Georgia Forestry Commission

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. Only the state list entry (coordinates, elevation 515, tag gfc-601, page revised March 2016) and the GFC history were usable. The list gives no unit for elevation; the story reads it as feet, which matches the brief's elevation_m of 157.0. The name 'macon' is the list author's own label, since entry 203 is above 72; it is not an official name and should not be presented as one. The gfc-601 tag matches the brief's 'GFC US 601' register number, but no source explains the tag. The GFC headquarters move to Macon in 1956 is context only; no source links it to this tower and the story does not imply a link. Two web searches found nothing on this tower's build, staffing, status or access. Not on NHLR or FFLOS in the local cache. Worth asking the Georgia Forestry Commission about the tower's history and whether it still stands.
